_about: HALO bone mineral density (BMD) thresholds, expressed as % of the crewmember's own pre-mission BMD so no absolute g/cm2 baseline is needed. NASA values are copied from the source; the 97% / 95% buffer lines are DERIVED by our team.

nasa_standard.source: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Revision C (2023-09-15), section 4.7, pages 39-40
nasa_standard.V1 4026_pre_mission: pre-mission BMD T-scores for total hip and lumbar spine (L1-L4) shall be consistent with an age, sex, gender, and ethnic-matched population (no numeric cut-off given)
nasa_standard.V1 4027_in_mission: Countermeasures shall maintain BMD of the hip and spine at or above 95% of pre-mission values, and at or above 90% for the femoral neck
nasa_standard.V1 4028_post_mission: reconditioning aimed at returning BMD to pre-mission baseline

halo_alert_rules.basis: act = below NASA V1 4027 (95%); watch = 2-point buffer (derived)
act = below NASA V1 4027 (90%); watch = 5-point buffer (derived)

simulation_parameters.source: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced Changes to Bone (2017), p.4 and Table 4 p.22
simulation_parameters.general_loss_pct_per_month: 1 to 1.5 (weight-bearing sites: hip, lumbar spine, lower limbs)
simulation_parameters.recovery: slower than the loss, asymptotic; can return to pre-flight as early as 6 months after landing (p.15, p.23)
simulation_parameters.secondary_check: Stavnichuk et al. 2020 npj Microgravity 6:13 meta-analysis (~148 astronauts): lower limbs -0.8%/month [-1.1, -0.5]; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7200725

note: On the ISS, BMD is measured by DXA/QCT before and after flight, not in flight. HALO's in-flight bone value is therefore an ESTIMATE from these rates (plus exercise compliance), and should be labelled as such in the demo.
